note: Monday 12 Oct 2026, 07:02 SGT -- before Asia's open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30 SGT), US Columbus Day (bond market closed, equities open normally later today). No new equity session has closed since Friday 9 Oct's US close, so equity-based metrics below (CNN fearGreed value/components, breadth, flows) remain Friday's confirmed figures, re-verified against fresh search this run rather than re-stamped blind. Crypto Fear&Greed was checked directly via alternative.me's API (not just the cached webpage): the latest posted daily reading is for Oct 11 00:00 UTC = 61 (Greed), identical to Sunday's run -- the next daily refresh (due ~08:00 SGT, i.e. shortly after this filing) had not posted yet, so despite crypto trading 24/7 there genuinely is no fresher number to report yet. CNN's own Fear&Greed API returned HTTP 418 to automated fetch; cross-checked mirrors (fearandgreedgraph.com, Benzinga) independently reconfirm Friday's close at 45, Neutral. Breadth: searched for anything newer than Friday's 41-highs-vs-120-lows read; found Trefis daily new-high/new-low counts (e.g. 13 highs vs 7 lows on Oct 9) that conflict with it, traced this to a methodology/universe mismatch (Trefis samples a restricted subset rather than the full S&P 500 count the baseline source uses) and rejected it rather than swapping it in blind -- no genuine fresher full-index print exists, so Friday's figures are carried forward unchanged. Flows: the week-ended-Wed-Oct-7 BofA Flow Show/EPFR print remains the latest published edition; the next weekly edition is still not due until ~Oct 15-16, confirmed via fresh search (no new edition found). What is genuinely new since Sunday: geopolitical rhetoric escalated further Sunday/Monday -- Trump posted that 'every shot fired by the Houthis' will now be treated as fired 'from the weapons and leadership of Iran' and that Iran will face 'dire' consequences (CNBC/Fox News, 11 Oct), building on Saturday's Riyadh airport strike already captured in the prior run; early-Monday-Asia wire color has oil holding above $100/bbl on the escalation and a broad gold/silver/platinum-group rally continuing into the Asia session (marketindex.com.au ASX preview), but no verified index or asset price levels were available to me this run, so none are stated as hard figures in the structured fields above what was already sourced Friday.

flows.period: week ending Wed Oct 7, 2026 (BofA Flow Show / EPFR Global, now confirmed -- a fuller report than Friday's preliminary approximations, superseding that file's guessed figures)
flows.narrative: The full BofA/EPFR weekly print landed with a much clearer and, in several cases, quite different picture than Friday's preliminary approximations. Headline: a record $166.4B flooded into money-market funds -- the largest weekly inflow since April 2020 -- with Hartnett framing it as structural cash-hoarding ('no rate cuts, no reduction in cash') rather than a classic flight-to-safety, since money funds already offer attractive yields. Bonds added $33.8B. Global equity funds still took in a net $12.4B even so: US equities swung back to a modest inflow (+$3.3B, first in three weeks), EM funds logged a second straight week of inflows (+$2.1B), helped by China-dedicated funds rebounding sharply as domestic investors returned from Golden Week, and Europe barely held positive (+$0.2B, second straight week). Japan was the standout loser, flipping to its biggest outflow since May (-$3.3B). Gold ETFs added a steady +$2.0B, continuing the record-setting 2026 run even as spot gold hit fresh highs Friday. Within US sectors, Technology funds took in $3.5B (largest in six weeks) while Financials saw their biggest outflow since March (-$3.0B). No newer weekly edition has been published as of Monday pre-open; the next one is expected ~Oct 15-16.
